title: Intersect calendar event spans before enumerating occupied dates
description:
## Finding

Calendar rendering and reminder expansion enumerate an event's entire lifetime before intersecting it with the requested date window. A hostile but syntactically valid event can therefore force an enormous allocation and CPU walk even when the UI requests only one month.

`CalEvent::dates_in` pushes every day from `DTSTART` through `DTEND` into a new `Vec`. The non-recurring `occurrences` path calls that function merely to test overlap, discarding the vector, and `expand_by_date` calls it again for the accepted occurrence. A multi-century event can walk and allocate hundreds of thousands of dates twice; dates near Chrono's representable extrema make the bound far larger. The final bucketing clones the complete event once per occupied date.

`calendar.max_events` limits source rows, not generated occurrences, occupied-date entries, aggregate bytes, or clones. Remote CalDAV/ICS URL and command sources can supply the span.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/thegn-core/src/calendar/mod.rs:284-304`: `dates_in` allocates every date across the untrusted full span.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/calendar/mod.rs:342-359`: non-recurring overlap detection expands that entire span.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/calendar/mod.rs:410-430`: bucketing expands the span again and clones each materialized event per matching date.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/config_calendar.rs:55-57`: the documented cap applies only to cached source events.

## Impact

A single feed record can monopolize the bounded background lane or exhaust memory, delaying calendar, tracker, Git, and other hydration work. A small requested display window does not bound the cost.

## Required implementation

* Test overlap by comparing resolved interval boundaries; never allocate occupied dates to decide whether an event intersects a window.
* Add a window-aware occupied-date iterator or equivalent that clamps to `[from, to]` before iteration.
* Use checked date/time arithmetic at representable boundaries and define malformed/inverted span behavior explicitly.
* Enforce one end-to-end expansion budget covering occurrences, occupied-date bucket entries, clones, and aggregate bytes. Do not silently return a plausible partial calendar; expose a typed partial/error state.
* Avoid cloning unbounded event payload strings per date where a shared occurrence representation can preserve the UI contract.
* Apply the same boundary to month rendering and reminder evaluation.

## Verification

Add adversarial tests for a one-day window intersecting century-scale and Chrono-boundary events, very large descriptions on multi-day events, events wholly outside the window, midnight-exclusive endings, inverted spans, recurrence instances with long duration, and aggregate exhaustion across many source rows. Assert work/allocation is proportional to the requested window and configured output budget.

## Dependencies

Dependency-ready. Coordinate the common expansion budget and failure model with <issue id="967e9fbc-0223-44de-ae42-2ccda1695505" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-457/bound-and-validate-recurrence-expansion-and-reminder-arithmetic">THE-457</issue>. Local-input byte admission remains owned by <issue id="0891b34e-9fcb-4d9c-8ee6-2a025d6d22c2" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-455/bound-and-determinize-local-ics-file-and-vdir-ingestion">THE-455</issue>.
